The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said a tank containing about 4.5m litres of fuel was directly hit, triggering a huge fire that caused it to collapse. It said it was considering suspending operations if the attacks continued. There were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation, Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said on Tuesday. The Zawiya refinery is the largest operational facility in Libya, with an output of 120,000 barrels per day. The NOC condemned similar attacks in past days in Zawiya, including two drone strikes on a naphtha reservoir and a water desalination plant. It called on the authorities to investigate who was behind the violence. Los Mirlos: Tiny Desk Concert September 17, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castillo/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Originally born from Afro-Colombian communities, cumbia spread across the Spanish-speaking world , acquiring distinct musical accents along the way. In Peru, cumbia became particularly popular among oil workers deep in the Amazon. And when Jorge Rodriguez Grández started Los Mirlos in his small hometown of Moyobamba, his band played a regional style called cumbia amazónica, easily identifiable by its electric, reverb-heavy, surf-rock guitar. Sponsor Message Alt.Latino Cumbia: The Musical Backbone Of Latin America Los Mirlos' time behind the Desk is not only a joyful celebration of this music but also a trail of small towns and cities throughout the Amazon jungle. Throughout their performance, these cultural ambassadors share stories and declare their love for cumbia and their tropical homeland. We are so fortunate to host and share with you a group of true pioneers and innovators who, over 50 years later, still effortlessly pump out cumbia grooves. First of all, it was the final production of our sixth annual El Tiny series. This was a very emotional moment for a lot of reasons. People really love Los Tigres del Norte, to the point that playing their albums feels like sitting with family. And if you’ve seen the introduction I gave the band just before they played at the desk you can see that I wasn’t embarrassed to get emotional when I talked about what the band means to me. That emotional intro led to some changes in our process and format that resulted in a huge response from the audience that went viral. The result was a messy moment behind the scenes here at NPR and more than a little confusion for a lot of you. This week’s episode looks back at last week. First we want to share with you, directly from us, an explanation of what happened. But mostly we want to put the spotlight back on the band and their music because for decades they have been bringing out the kind emotions that got this whole thing started. pages.text: Man with venomous snakes and lizards stopped at German airport Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Man with suitcase full of snakes stopped at German airport 15 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Paulin Kola German Customs Not all the the snakes and lizards were alive, officials said A man has been stopped at Cologne Bonn Airport in Germany after trying to smuggle in more than 90 lizards and venomous snakes. Customs officials said the 45-year-old Mexican firefighter had looked "conspicuously nervous" as he tried to go through the green - nothing to declare - exit at the airport. They conducted a drugs test on the man - which came back positive for cocaine - before proceeding to check his suitcase. They did not find any drugs, but vipers, rattlesnakes and other species of snakes and lizards, including iguanas, hidden in shampoo and cream bottles, plastic containers and balls of socks. "My colleagues at the airport are used to a lot when it comes to souvenirs in suitcases, but we've never had 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards from Mexico before," said Jens Ahland, spokesman for the Cologne Customs office. Some were being kept "in inhumane conditions", Ahland said. Others had died during the journey from Mexico City via Istanbul. The man, who has not been named, told officers that he had brought the animals back as a favour for a Brazilian acquaintance. He was denied entry to Germany and flown back to Istanbul. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Manatee Awareness Month: Protecting Gentle Giants at the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse Outstanding Natural Area Nov 3, 2026 Every November, Manatee Awareness Month celebrates one of Florida’s most beloved residents: the West Indian manatee. Often called “sea cows” because of their grazing habits, these gentle giants can grow to more than 10 feet long and weigh over 1,000 pounds. Despite their impressive size, manatees are peaceful, slow-moving animals that spend much of their time feeding on aquatic vegetation, resting, and traveling through coastal waters, rivers, estuaries, and springs. West Indian manatees swim in the clear, shallow waters of the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse Outstanding Natural Area in Jupiter, Florida. The Bureau of Land Management site is the only BLM-managed area where manatees are regularly observed and provides important habitat for these gentle marine mammals. pages.text: Mario Balotelli: Why always him? The rise and fall of the Italian striker - BBC Sport By Jess Anderson BBC Sport journalist Maverick. Loose cannon. Unmanageable. Mario Balotelli heard it all. Perhaps better known for off-field antics than his undeniable - yet arguably wasted - talent with the ball at his feet, the Italian has always attracted headlines. Fifteen years have passed since his famous 'Why always me?' Manchester derby T-shirt celebration, which came just days after a firework was set off in his own bathroom, causing a house fire. The 36-year-old is still playing, now in the United Arab Emirates first division with Al-Ittifaq alongside his biological brother, Enock Barwuah. Here, BBC Sport looks at a career that has included 13 clubs, six countries - and an assist for arguably the most famous goal in Premier League history. Mancini to Mourinho - cracks begin to show Typical of his unconventional footballing life, Balotelli's career did not begin in an elite club's academy. Instead, by his mid-teens he was turning out for Italian third-tier side Lumezzane, close to the family home in Concesio. A trial at Barcelona did not lead to a long-term stay, and instead he was picked up by Inter Milan in 2006. It was at Inter that Balotelli first came across his great mentor - Roberto Mancini. The relationship between the two has been likened to that of a father and son. Under the Italian coach's tutelage, Balotelli flourished. pages.text: Mary Anning: The forgotten fossil hunter who transformed Britain’s Jurassic Coast | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH The forgotten fossil hunter who transformed Britain’s Jurassic Coast Mary Anning and her most important dinosaur finds went unsung, but her legacy now draws travelers to southwest England. London‘s Natural History Museum displays several of Mary Anning‘s remarkable fossil finds, including this one of an ichthyosaur (lower). Photograph by Tommy Trenchard, Panos Pictures/Redux By Cathy Newman Published March 29, 2021 • 11 min read If you had lived in Victorian times, you’d have spotted her, perhaps, at the foot of Church Cliff to the east of Lyme Regis, a seaside town on England’s southwest coast. She’d have a wicker basket in one hand, a small geologist’s hammer in the other, and be dressed in a plaid coat and cape made of heavy wool—it is chilly by the shore. Her small dog, Tray, would have been skittering by her side. Self-taught paleontologist Mary Anning would search for fossils along the Dorset coast, accompanied by her dog, Tray. Photograph by GL Archive, Alamy Stock Photo What you might not have known then is that Mary Anning was arguably the greatest fossil hunter of them all, “the princess of paleontology,” a contemporary called her. In Victorian England, in an era of amateur scientists, fossil hunters were nearly always men. Anning was born in Lyme Regis, which sits on one of the great fossil deposits from the Jurassic era.
